summary: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire collapse sent oil prices higher this week, keeping rate-hike expectations elevated — market expectations for a Fed hike at the July FOMC jumped to 31% from 17%, and September probability surged to 84% from 61% week-over-week. A below-consensus PPI report Wednesday briefly pulled Treasury yields lower, with the 10-year settling near 4.55%, easing immediate tightening fears.
tweet: Iran conflict reigniting rate-hike bets — July FOMC hike probability doubled this week — while blowout Q2 earnings keep stocks in greed and bonds under pressure.
